implementation_notes: Rust is unusually well equipped: `cargo check` reports dead code, `#[warn(dead_code)]` covers unused fields and methods, and the `unused_crate_dependencies` lint reports Cargo.toml entries nothing imports. The idiom to avoid is `#[allow(dead_code)]`: it is the standard way a codebase silences the signal permanently, and a review that accepts it without asking converts a finding into an anchor. Feature-gated code is the other blind spot — a function behind a feature nothing enables is dead in every real configuration, and the default-feature build will not tell you.
idiom_name: unused `pub` item; unused crate in Cargo.toml; `#[allow(dead_code)]`
pitfalls: `#[allow(dead_code)]` silences the compiler and is almost always permanent; require a justification or a removal date.
Code behind a disabled cargo feature is dead in practice and invisible in the default build.
`pub` in a library crate makes an item reachable from outside, so rustc will not report it even when no downstream consumer uses it.
